summary:
This evaluation covered three chat-task evals related to SageMaker endpoint diagnostics, run 3 times each for both variants (15 total iterations, no run failures).

1. "endpoint-slow-and-erroring": The trigger_fired check (measured once, not per-variant) failed in all 3 runs (0/3), meaning the underlying behavior under test never fired for either variant in this eval. Because of that, expected_output also failed for both without_skill and with_skill (0/3 each), and all 7 per-assertion checks came back "inconclusive" for both variants (null results) rather than pass or fail — essentially no usable assertion-level data was produced here. No quality comparison pairs could be evaluated (all 3 were skipped), and output consistency is unknown for both. Runtime and cost were negligible (~0s, $0.00) for both, which itself suggests the task likely short-circuited rather than running a full diagnostic flow. This eval is essentially a non-result for differentiating the variants — the trigger/behavior itself didn't fire, so nothing meaningful can be concluded about without_skill vs with_skill from it.

2. "idle-endpoint-wasting-money": Same pattern — trigger_fired was 0/3, and expected_output failed for both variants (0/3, medium confidence). Unlike the first eval, assertions here did resolve to real pass/fail results rather than "inconclusive," but every one of the 6 assertions (covering checks like distinguishing no-datapoints from measured zero, treating empty scalable-targets correctly, using safe recommend-only remediation language, including a catalog check-id, and not exposing account IDs) failed for both without_skill and with_skill (always_fails pattern, 0/12 total assertions each, high confidence on most). This is a case where both variants failed identically — the assertions and/or the underlying task scenario appear not to be met by either system, not a case where one variant underperformed the other. Runtime and cost were close and small (without_skill: ~10s/$0.09; with_skill: ~9s/$0.08), a negligible difference. No quality-comparison pairs were evaluated (all 3 skipped), and output consistency data is unavailable for both variants.

3. "negative-serverless-cold-start": This is a negative-trigger eval (should_trigger: false), and trigger_fired was 3/3 (100%) as expected for this design, meaning the agent correctly did NOT fire the tested behavior in 3/3 runs. All downstream measurements (expected_output, assertions, metrics, comparison, consistency) were intentionally skipped since the eval doesn't apply to those dimensions. This is a clean, unremarkable pass-through with no variant-level data to compare.

Overall state: Across all three evals, there is no dimension where without_skill and with_skill diverge — every comparable metric (trigger behavior, expected-output pass rate, assertion pass rate, runtime, cost) is either identical or shows both variants failing or succeeding together. No quality-comparison pairs were evaluable in any eval, and no output-consistency data exists for either variant. The two evals with substantive assertion data ("endpoint-slow-and-erroring" and "idle-endpoint-wasting-money") indicate the underlying trigger condition and/or expected-output criteria were not met by either variant, suggesting the test scenarios themselves (or the behaviors they're probing) may need review rather than indicating any difference between the two agent variants. No conclusions can be drawn about which variant performs better, because the data shows no differentiation — both either fully failed or fully passed together on every measured dimension.

endpoint-slow-and-erroring.summary:
This evaluation did not produce usable data for comparing with_skill and without_skill. The trigger that was supposed to initiate the test behavior did not fire in any of the 3 runs (0/3), meaning the underlying scenario never actually executed as intended. As a direct consequence, every downstream measurement is empty or inconclusive:

- Expected output: both with_skill and without_skill show 0/3 pass rate, but since the trigger never fired, this reflects the absence of a valid test condition rather than a quality failure by either variant.
- Per-assertion results: all 7 assertions (covering check-id grounding, metric namespace reads, EndpointStatus interpretation, non-mutating remediation guidance, handling of missing datapoints, LLM-SM catalog check-id presence, and account ID redaction) are marked "inconclusive" for both variants — none of these assertions actually discriminated between the two systems, because there was no valid output to assess.
- Quality comparison: 0 pairs were evaluated and all 3 pairs were skipped, so no head-to-head quality judgment exists between the variants.
- Runtime and cost: both variants show ~0s runtime and $0.00 cost, which is consistent with the task not actually running rather than a meaningful efficiency finding.
- Context window utilization was nearly identical (with_skill 4.3% vs without_skill 4.2%), a negligible difference not meaningful on its own given the lack of real task execution.
- Output consistency: no data recorded for either variant.

Overall, this is an absent-data situation rather than a performance finding: the triggering condition for the test never activated, so no conclusions can be drawn about either variant's behavior, quality, correctness, or efficiency on this eval. The results should be treated as inconclusive/not run rather than as evidence that either variant underperformed.

per_assertion.text: The response reports findings grounded in the LLM-SM check family with explicit check-ids rather than generic advice
The response reads both metric namespaces (AWS/SageMaker invocation metrics and /aws/sagemaker/Endpoints instance resource metrics) before stating any right-sizing conclusion
The response treats EndpointStatus InService as control-plane state only and confirms serving from CurrentInstanceCount and recent Invocations rather than assuming InService means serving traffic

Every remediation is presented as a recommendation with the command for the operator to run, and the response does not call or claim to have called any mutating API such as UpdateEndpoint or UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities
The response states what it actually observed for each signal, including explicitly saying when a metric returned no datapoints rather than treating absence as a measured zero
At least one finding carries an LLM-SM catalog check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

idle-endpoint-wasting-money.summary:
Both variants performed identically on every measured dimension in this eval, and that shared result was uniformly negative.

- Trigger/expected output: The behavior under test did not fire in any of the 3 runs (0/3) for either variant, and expected_output also failed 0/3 for both, at medium confidence. This means the core scenario this eval is checking for essentially never materialized for either agent, so this eval provides little evidence of a difference between them — it's more a sign the trigger condition or task setup needs review.

- Assertions: All 12 assertions failed for both with_skill and without_skill (0/12 each), and every one of the 6 underlying assertion checks shows an "always_fails" pattern for both variants (checking for CurrentInstanceCount/Invocations usage, distinguishing no-datapoints from measured zero, correct interpretation of empty scalable-targets results, recommending remediation without self-executing mutating calls, including an LLM-SM catalog check-id, and not exposing raw account IDs). Confidence on these assertion judgments is high for most and medium for one (the remediation-as-command assertion), so these failures are reasonably well-established, but since neither variant passes any of them, these assertions discriminate nothing between the two — they point to a shared gap in behavior rather than a relative weakness of one variant.

- Quality comparison: No pairs could be evaluated (0 pairs evaluated, 3 skipped), so there is no quality-based signal distinguishing the variants in this eval.

- Runtime/cost: with_skill averaged ~9s and $0.08 per run; without_skill averaged ~10s and $0.09 per run. These are very small differences (about 1 second and $0.01) and context window utilization was identical (4.4%, 0 compactions) for both — not a meaningful distinguishing factor.

- Output consistency: Not available (null) for both variants, so run-to-run stability cannot be assessed here.

Overall, this eval shows no differentiation between with_skill and without_skill: both failed to trigger the expected behavior, both failed all assertions identically, no quality comparison was possible, and cost/runtime differences were negligible. The most notable takeaway is not a comparison between the agents but that the underlying scenario/trigger and all associated checks failed for both, suggesting the eval itself (or the behavior it targets) needs further investigation before it can meaningfully differentiate the two variants.
